title: Shiv Om Pandey v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
coram: Sangeeta Chandra, J. and Brij Raj Singh, J.
disposition: Fresh speaking assessment after objections; demand kept in abeyance.
headnote: On a meter-bypass demand of Rs.4,34,633, the Lucknow Bench directed the assessing officer to consider objections the consumer said he had sent by registered post and to pass a fresh reasoned and speaking final assessment within two weeks, keeping the demand notice in abeyance for four weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier.
facts: Shiv Om Pandey took a house connection in 2017. It was disconnected on 17 January 2023 for dues of Rs.19,381, which he paid with reconnection charges. A letter of 8 February 2023, based on a checking report of 18 January 2023 that the prayer linked to his brother's premises, alleged meter-bypass theft. He said objections posted on 22 February 2023 were ignored. A demand of 3 August 2024 sought Rs.4,34,633. The licensee said a final assessment of 23 January 2024 had issued and the objections were never received.

holding_units.topic: Theft assessment: consider posted objections and pass a fresh speaking final order
holding_units.holding: Where the consumer asserts that objections to a provisional meter-bypass assessment were sent by registered post and the licensee denies receipt, the assessing officer must consider those objections and pass a fresh reasoned and speaking final assessment; the demand notice remains in abeyance until that decision or for four weeks, whichever is earlier.

principle_tags.application: The meter-bypass allegation was sent back so that objections the consumer said were posted on 22 February 2023 would be considered before a fresh reasoned and speaking final assessment, with the demand kept in abeyance in the meantime.

not_decided.point: Whether section 126(3) was breached for want of a final assessment within thirty days of the provisional order
not_decided.note: Counsel said only a demand notice had issued. The licensee said an assessment dated 23 January 2024 had issued. The Court did not decide that dispute.

not_decided.point: Whether clause 6.8(b)(i) or clause 8.1(b) governed, and whether the bypass allegation and the demand of Rs.4,34,633 were justified
not_decided.note: Both clauses were invoked. The Court directed a fresh assessment without a finding on the applicable clause or on the merits.
